title: Iranian attack injures eight United States Marines
seoTitle: Iranian attack injures eight United States Marines
subtitle: Incident occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and was not disclosed by the Department of Defense
excerpt: Eight U.S. Marines were injured after an Iranian cruise‑missile attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Eight United States Marines were injured after an Iranian cruise‑missile attack on a ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The incident added to a growing tally of wounded troops amid recent regional conflicts.

The attack in the Strait of Hormuz

The episode occurred while the vessel was navigating the waterway. The group hit consisted of seven enlisted personnel and one officer who were part of a battalion landing team. The service members were not aboard a U.S. Navy ship, and authorities did not specify the exact type of vessel involved.

Severity of the injuries

Despite the cruise‑missile strike, the Marines did not sustain serious injuries. Affected personnel reported inhaling smoke and concussion‑like symptoms, such as headaches, indicating possible traumatic brain injury. All eight returned to duty shortly after the incident.

Initial lack of Pentagon disclosure

The Department of Defense had not publicly disclosed any attack in September or the injuries sustained by the service members. The episode only emerged later through reports based on official sources. The defense’s casualty‑analysis system added the eight Marines to the list of wounded designated for overseas operations days after the event.

Casualty and wounded counts in the war

These injuries increase the total number of service members affected in connection with the conflict involving Iran. The Pentagon updated the public count of wounded troops in the war, while the official casualty‑analysis system recorded the total number of injured personnel during operations. Official sources explained that there can be temporal gaps in injury reports because symptoms are not always reported immediately and the system is not updated in real time.

With information from The Jerusalem Post, AOL.com.
